I’ll inspect the project policies and the smallest relevant frontend/server configuration surface, then patch only the OpenAI server integration and brand tokens. I will not start any runtime or modify dependency manifests.

The project already has a backend entry point, so this is a focused integration repair rather than a new server scaffold. I’m tracing the current API call, configuration error path, and CSS tokens before editing.

The failure is caused by the frontend sending `/api` requests to Vite without a proxy, even though `backend/src/server.js` already implements the OpenAI routes. I’ll connect that existing server path, make disconnected-server status distinct from missing API configuration, and tighten the existing SaaS Momentum overrides. I also found live-looking credentials in `.env.example`; I’ll replace those example values with blanks while leaving the real `.env` untouched.

The server route is now wired through the frontend proxy, Docker resolves that proxy to the existing backend service, and the UI distinguishes “server unavailable” from “API key not configured.” I’m running static syntax and diff checks only, per the no-runtime constraint.

Implemented the scoped update:

- Connected frontend `/api` requests to the existing backend server.
- Added Docker backend proxy routing.
- Improved server/OpenAI status messaging.
- Applied accessible SaaS Momentum brand colors.
- Removed credentials from `.env.example`; `.env` remains untouched.
- Static JavaScript checks passed.

No runtime servers were started. Unrelated functionality was preserved.
